issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may dissolve a marriage under Article 142(1) on the ground of irretrievable breakdown despite one spouse’s opposition, where the facts establish that the marriage has completely failed and reconciliation is not possible.

Whether irretrievable breakdown of marriage exists must be determined on the facts of each case by assessing the relationship holistically and considering relevant, non-exhaustive factors, rather than by deciding which spouse was at fault.

A spouse’s entitlement to permanent alimony must be determined by a case-specific assessment of relevant circumstances and cannot be based simply on equalising wealth with the other spouse or matching what a former spouse received.
The Court may quash criminal proceedings arising from matrimonial disputes when granting a divorce under Article 142(1) to do complete justice between the parties.
